'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***Intense fighting between [[Taliban]] [[insurgent]]s and [[government of Afghanistan|government]] [[Afghan Armed Forces|forces]] kills 28 civilians and injures another 290 during the past week, according to the head of a hospital in [[Kunduz Province|Kunduz]], with the majority of the dead being children, women and elderly people. The Taliban has moved beyond its southern strongholds and has intensified the fighting in the north, according to [[military]] experts. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/twenty-eight-civilians-killed-northern-afghan-province-fighting-intensifies-2021-06-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Federal Ministry of Defence (Germany)|German Defense Minister]] [[Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer]] announces that [[Germany]] has completed the withdrawal of [[Bundeswehr|its troops]] from [[Afghanistan]], thereby ending its involvement in the war. [https://sputniknews.com/world/202106291083268979-germany-removes-all-troops-from-afghanistan-ends-20-year-military-stay/ (Sputnik News)]
**The last [[Italian Army|Italian troops]] leave Afghanistan after handing over their base in [[Herat]] to Afghan security forces, thereby ending [[Italy]]'s involvement in the war. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/06/29/last-german-troops-leave-afghanistan-after-nearly-20-years-deployed (Euronews)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] and [[Tigray Defense Forces]] pledge to "drive enemies out" of the regional capital [[Mekelle]] after a unilateral ceasefire was declared by Ethiopia on Monday. Tigrayan forces say that the city of Mekelle is completely under the control of their forces. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/29/tigray-rebels-vow-to-drive-out-enemies-despite-ceasefire (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Eritrean Defence Forces|Eritrean troops]] withdraw from the towns of [[Adwa]], [[Axum]], and [[Shire Inda Selassie|Shire]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/eritrean-forces-withdraw-from-key-towns-in-ethiopia-s-tigray-1.5489829 (CTV News)]
**After seizing the regional capital, [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] spokesman [[Getachew Reda]] states that Tigrayan forces would invade the neighbouring [[Amhara Region]] and [[Eritrea]] to "destroy the enemy", claiming that the enemy, "whether from the Eritrean side or Amhara side or [[Addis Ababa]], doesn't have the capability to threaten the security of our people anymore". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-57645282 (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials]], [[House Resolution 3005]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] votes 285–120 on a bill to remove [[Confederate States Army|Confederate]] statues from the [[United States Capitol]], as well as replacing the bust of [[Chief Justice of the United States|Chief Justice]] [[Roger B. Taney]], known for the pro-slavery ''[[Dred Scott v. Sandford]]'' ruling, with one of [[Associate Justice of the Supreme Court of the United States|Associate Justice]] [[Thurgood Marshall]], the first Black justice on the court. The bill will head to the [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/29/house-votes-to-remove-confederate-statues-from-capitol.html (CNBC)] 

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Minister of Transport (Canada)|Canadian Transport Minister]] [[Omar Alghabra]] announces that by 2035, all new cars and [[light truck]]s sold in the country have to be [[Zero-emissions vehicle|zero-emission]]. The target, previously set for 2040 for all passenger vehicles, was moved up after a recent report by the [[International Energy Agency]] said that to achieve net zero-emissions by mid-century, all new light vehicle sales had to be electric. [https://financialpost.com/commodities/energy/electric-vehicles/liberals-say-by-2035-all-new-cars-light-duty-trucks-sold-in-canada-will-be-electric (''Financial Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Western North America heat wave]]
**More than 130 people die in [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]], and six more across the [[United States]] due to the extreme hot temperatures that are affecting the country. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57654133 (BBC News)]
**The temperature reaches {{convert|49.6|C|F}} in [[Lytton, British Columbia]], breaking the all-time record for hottest temperature ever recorded in Canada for the third day in a row. The temperature reached  {{convert|47.6|C|F}} in Lytton on June 28 and {{convert|46.6|C|F}} on June 27, both records. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/canada-bc-alberta-heat-wave-heat-dome-temperature-records-1.6084203 (CBC)] 

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] surpasses 900,000 cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://thefinancialexpress.com.bd/national/total-coronavirus-cases-in-bangladesh-top-900000-1624968654?amp=true (''The Financial Express'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****The [[Drugs Controller General of India]] grants emergency use approval for the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] imported by [[Cipla]]. [https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/cipla-gets-nod-to-import-moderna-s-covid-vaccine-for-emergency-use-in-india/amp-11624959964096.html (Livemint)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports its first cases of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] with more than 10 people detected in [[Mashhad]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/coronavirus-delta-variant-detected-for-first-time-in-iran/2289021 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] further closes its borders, allowing only 600 entries per day, in an attempt to reduce the spread of the [[Delta variant]] as the country has so far reported over 4.4 million cases and more than 93,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.adndigital.com.py/argentina-cierra-sus-fronteras-contra-la-variante-delta-de-coronavirus/ (ADN Digital)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Perth]], [[Brisbane]] and their respective surrounding towns enter lockdown as coronavirus spreads from the [[Sydney]] cluster. People will only be allowed to leave home for essential work or study, medical or compassionate reasons, essential shopping, or outdoor exercise (with restrictions), and masks must be worn outdoors. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-06-28/wa-coronavirus-perth-peel-hard-lockdown/100250920 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record 652 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 134,545. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/06/29/russia-breaks-daily-coronavirus-fatality-record-a74370 (''The Moscow Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] reports a record 5,251 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, prompting the [[Government of Tunisia|government]] to extend the curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. beginning from July 1. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tunisia-extends-curfew-hours-reports-daily-record-5251-covid-19-cases-2021-06-29/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] imposes a curfew from 6:30 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., bans inter-city travel, and reduces business hours to 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. in response to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/zimbabwe-imposes-dusk-dawn-curfew-new-covid-19-restrictions-2021-06-29/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***A study shows that the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] developed by [[Moderna]] is effective against [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variants]] including the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/29/moderna-says-covid-vaccine-shows-promise-in-a-lab-setting-against-variants-including-delta.html (CNBC)]
***[[White House Press Secretary|U.S. White House Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] announces that the [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] will [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines|ship]] 2 million doses of the [[Pfizer]] [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to [[Peru]] and 2.5 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|Moderna vaccine]] to [[Pakistan]]. Additionally, the [[United States]] will also send vaccine doses to [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/biden-administration-send-covid-vaccines-peru-pakistan-2021-06-28/ (Reuters)] [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/us-sending-bangladesh-25-million-covid-19-vaccine-doses-white-house (''The Straits Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Israel)|Israel Foreign Minister]] [[Yair Lapid]] visits the [[United Arab Emirates]], making it the first visit to the country by an [[Israel]] government official since the two countries [[Israel–United Arab Emirates normalization agreement|normalized relations]] nine months ago. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/29/israeli-fm-inaugurates-embassy-in-the-uae-in-first-official-visit (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Kosovo–Serbia relations]]
**In an interview with the [[Serbia]]n division of [[Euronews]], [[President of Serbia|Serbian President]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] says that any hopes of his country reclaiming [[Kosovo]] is unrealistic, and that he is willing to enter a "rational and compromise solution" regarding recognition of Kosovo's independence. However, he says that any agreement reached between the two countries needs to ultimately be decided by referendum. [https://exit.al/en/2021/06/30/serbia-to-hold-referendum-over-any-potential-agreement-with-kosovo/ (''Exit.al'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Constitutional Court of South Africa]] finds former [[President of South Africa|President]] [[Jacob Zuma]] guilty of [[contempt of court]] over his refusal to answer questions on [[corruption in South Africa|corruption]] [[criminal charge|charge]]s and [[sentence (law)|sentences]] him to 15 months' imprisonment. [https://www.dw.com/en/jacob-zuma-south-africa-jails-ex-president-for-15-months/a-58087446 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Vanuatu]]
**[[Prime Minister of Vanuatu|Prime Minister]] [[Bob Loughman]] wins a confidence vote by the [[Parliament of Vanuatu|parliament]] after a no-confidence motion had been introduced to remove his [[government of Vanuatu|government]] by opposition leader [[Ralph Regenvanu]]. However, Loughman's hold on power remains tenuous as the Supreme Court ruled earlier this month that the seats of 19 government MPs were to be declared vacant. Loughman's government has already appealed the ruling. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/445732/vanuatu-pm-wins-confidence-vote (RNZ)]
*[[2021 Eswatini protests]]
**Acting [[List of prime ministers of Eswatini|Prime Minister]] [[Themba Masuku]] denies reports that [[List of monarchs of Eswatini|King]] [[Mswati III]] has fled [[Eswatini|the country]] amid ongoing nationwide protests. [https://www.news24.com/news24/southafrica/news/protests-rock-eswatini-govt-denies-reports-that-king-mswati-fled-20210629 (News24)] [http://www.swazilandnews.co.za/fundza.php?nguyiphi=1304 (Swaziland News)]
